funders.name: American Institute of Bangladesh Studies (AIBS) — Travel Grants for Bangladesh Citizens
funders.eligibility: Bangladeshi citizens who are PhD candidates or faculty members affiliated with an AIBS partner university in Bangladesh, presenting Bangladesh Studies research at a US conference.
funders.amount_note: Lump sum of up to USD 2,500 per grantee for international travel costs (airfare, ground transport, meals, lodging)
funders.source_quote: We are not accepting applications at the moment.
funders.notes: Directly on-topic (Bangladesh Studies) and covers a real US-travel gap, but the application window is closed as of this check; re-check aibs.net before relying on it.

funders.name: University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) — Research Grant Portal
funders.eligibility: Faculty at Bangladeshi public and private universities submitting a research project proposal through the UGC portal.
funders.cycle: Rolling online portal; specific international-conference-travel provisions not confirmed
funders.notes: UGC is the apex higher-education funding body in Bangladesh and runs a live research-grants portal, but no page was found confirming a dedicated international-conference-travel line; check with the home institution's UGC liaison office before assuming coverage.

funders.name: Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program (Bangladesh)
funders.eligibility: Senior Bangladeshi faculty/researchers with a PhD (or equivalent) and at least 10 years of professional experience, with a confirmed invitation from a US host institution.
funders.amount_note: 6-9 month research grant or 1-2 semester lecturing grant; specific stipend not stated on the page found
funders.notes: Not a conference-travel grant but a longer research/lecturing stay; the 10-year-experience bar may be a stretch for a single lecturer. Watch for the 2027-28 cycle announcement, expected via bd.usembassy.gov.

funders.name: CIES UREAG Travel Grant
funders.eligibility: CIES members, with a UREAG (Under-Represented and Emerging Areas Group) focus; typically graduate students and early-career members presenting at the CIES annual conference.
funders.cycle: Opens ahead of each CIES annual conference; check members.cies.us for the current-year window
funders.source_quote: This travel grant is generously funded by CIES in support of the UREAG Committee
funders.notes: Small but real, tied to CIES's own conference; requires CIES membership.

funders.name: CIES SAIS SIG Research Grant
funders.eligibility: Advanced graduate students and tenure-track faculty in the South Asia-focused special interest group of CIES.
funders.cycle: Annual; check cies-sais.org for the current call
funders.source_quote: The CIES SAIS SIG offers a scholastic research grant of up to $500 for advanced graduate students and tenure track faculty.
funders.notes: Directly relevant: South Asia special interest group of the flagship comparative-education society, open to faculty.

funders.name: BAICE Conference Bursaries
funders.eligibility: Colleagues at academic institutions in OECD 'least developed', 'low income' or 'lower middle income' countries (Bangladesh qualifies), or UK-based students/early-career researchers.
funders.amount_note: GBP 1,500 for applicants from lower-income countries; GBP 1,000 less for UK-based students/ECRs (GBP 500)
funders.cycle: Tied to the biennial BAICE conference (2026 round closed 25 May 2026, noon UK time); next round expected ahead of the following BAICE conference
funders.notes: The 2026-conference round has closed, but this is a recurring scheme worth re-checking ahead of the next BAICE conference; reimbursement-based, needs an acceptance letter and a letter confirming no institutional funding.
